title: Environment: uv, a script, a traceback

concept.heading: A Python project is a folder with a lockfile and a way to run things
paragraphs: uv manages the Python version, the virtual environment, and the dependencies for the middleware/ folder from one file, pyproject.toml. You never activate anything by hand: uv run python ... runs inside the right environment every time, on every machine, including a client's.

The first program in this track does one thing a connector does: call an HTTP endpoint, parse JSON, and hand one field onward. It also fails on purpose once, so you read a traceback from the bottom up and then make the failure a clean exit code instead of a crash.

That last part is the habit of the whole track. A middleware layer meets failures constantly: a 404, a timeout, a missing field. Each one is an expected outcome with a name, not an exception that escapes to the person asking.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: This is the HTTP action in Make or Power Automate with a parse-JSON step after it, plus the run history you read when it fails. In code, the run history is the traceback and the exit code.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: running a module and reading a traceback
pythonBlock.intro: A file under a package runs with python -m package.module. When it crashes, read the last line first (the error), then the nearest line in your own file.
pythonBlock.code:
uv run python -m hello.fetch_api http://127.0.0.1:8001/health --field status

# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "hello/fetch_api.py", line 31, in main
#     response.raise_for_status()
# httpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '404 Not Found' ...
#
# Bottom line: what went wrong. Nearest line in YOUR file: where to handle it.

resource.label: uv docs - Running scripts and projects

spec: Run uv sync inside middleware/ once; it creates .venv and installs the core dependencies.
Start the mock CRM in a second terminal: uv run python -m mock_services crm --port 8001.
Implement main(argv) so that uv run python -m hello.fetch_api <url> --field <name> prints one JSON line {url, field, value}.
A missing field exits 2 with {"error": "missing_field", "field": "<name>"} on stderr; a non-2xx response exits 1 with error: HTTP <status> on stderr and no traceback.
Try it against a public JSON API too (any that needs no key), then against the CRM.
askClaudeFor: The argparse skeleton: url positional, --field option.
writeYourself: The try/except that turns an HTTPStatusError into exit code 1 and a one-line message.
The field lookup and the JSON line printed to stdout.

check.command: uv run --directory middleware python checks/run.py m0-1-environment
check.summary: Runs your script as a subprocess against the mock CRM: prints the field as JSON, exits 2 on a missing field, exits 1 with no traceback on a 404.
